title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC1RA_1LD0LC_1LA0LA_1RA0RF_0RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC1RA_1LD0LC_1LA0LA_1RA0RF_0RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A two-level counter on words 0 1^(odd): the run of 1s at the right end grows by 2 per round in doubling time while a carry moves left through the word; full rewrites at 1.4e7 and 5.2e8 steps; open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 227 cells have been visited and 121 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Three rounds of the run, for any tape further left
claims.text: Three consecutive rounds of the run from blank tape (between moments the head is in A on the first 0 right of everything written), each proved for every tape left of the cells it visits, with its exact step count.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>9</sup> steps; rebuilds
claims.text: Direct simulation. The fast counter is the run 1^(2k) at the right end: it grows by 2 per round (by 4 between the samples shown), and each round takes twice as long as the one before plus about 2 steps. The slow list was rebuilt at about 1.4·107 and 5.2·108 steps (the head reaches the left end of the tape); between rebuilds each round makes one local change in it.

claims.title: Two-level counter
claims.text: Left of the fast counter is a slow list, a word in a, b, c, d, e: blocks of odd length separated by single 0s. In each round one local change happens in it, a little further left each time (a carry: for example c a^3 → b a b a^2, b^3 → a^2 b^2), so the list behaves like the low digits of a slow counter whose digits are the odd block lengths. When the change reaches the left end, the head sweeps the whole tape: going left, state C erases runs of 1s and the tape is rewritten into words 1^2 0^k, and going right it is rewritten back, a rebuild that makes the list longer. This pair shares the first rows 1RB0RE_1LC1RA_1LD0LC and differs in D0 and E1; both behave in the same way. Not shown for all sizes.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. See the heuristic claims above for what a halt would need.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LB0LB_0RB--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RA_1RC0RC_1LD0LE_1RA1LC_1LC0LF_0LC--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RB_1LC0LE_1RD1LB_1RA0RD_1LB0LF_0LB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a two-level counter: a fast counter at the right end of the tape needs twice as long for each round, and each round makes one small change in a slow list of blocks on its left; rarely the slow list is rebuilt. This page runs the machine and shows the rounds.

facts.text: Rounds of the run proved in Lean for any tape further left.
Each round twice as long as the one before.

sections.heading: A fast counter and a slow list
html: Look at the tape each time the head is in state A on the first blank cell right of everything written. Read the tape as words a = 01, b = 0111, c = 011111, d = 0 1^7, e = 0 1^9 (a 0 followed by an odd run of 1s) and z = 00; a^4 is four a's. The fast counter is the run 1^(2k) at the right end: it grows by 2 per round (by 4 between the samples shown), and each round takes twice as long as the one before plus about 2 steps.

sections.heading: Why it is hard to settle
html: The machine can halt only on its one undefined transition. The regular rounds are proved in Lean for three instances (for every tape further left) and behave the same way in every round seen; a halt could only come from a rebuild of the slow list (seen at about 1.4·107 and 5.2·108 steps (the head reaches the left end of the tape)). Rebuilds come after exponentially many rounds, and their rule is not known for all sizes, so the run cannot be followed beyond direct simulation. Since every rebuild seen made the list longer, the machine looks like it runs forever, but that is an extrapolation.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.019). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.064).
After 109 steps the tape spans 227 cells (33 left of the start, 193 right), with a density of 1s of 0.533.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
